<SYSTEM>This is the full developer documentation for Paladin Recruiter Help</SYSTEM>

# Quickstart

> Get started with Paladin Recruiter. Set up your account, make your first call, and see how the recruiting workflow fits together.

Paladin Recruiter is where you keep your candidates and jobs, and where your calls with candidates happen. Start a call from Paladin, and it prepares a brief beforehand, listens while you talk, and files the summary on the candidate’s record afterwards.

## How it works

[Section titled “How it works”](#how-it-works)

1. **Candidates and jobs live in Paladin.** Each candidate has a record with their résumé, notes, and every call you’ve had with them.
2. **You call from your own phone.** Start a call in Paladin and it rings your phone, then connects you to the candidate. Away from your desk, the Paladin Dialer app does the same from your phone. Either way the call is transcribed and the candidate sees your Paladin number.
3. **Paladin does the write-up.** While you talk, the Call Console shows the transcript and suggests questions. When you hang up, the summary goes onto the candidate’s record, under the job you called about.

## Get started

[Section titled “Get started”](#get-started)

For the whole loop, from a new job to a report for the hiring manager, see [The recruiting workflow](get-started/the-recruiting-workflow/).

1. **Set up your account.** Sign in with your invite and set the phone that rings, your caller ID name, and your password. [Set up your account](get-started/set-up-your-account/)
2. **Make your first call.** Open a candidate and select **Call Candidate**. [Call a candidate](calls/call-a-candidate/)
3. **Optional: install the Paladin Dialer** to call from your phone’s contacts and see calls live on your phone. [Install the Paladin Dialer](dialer/install-the-dialer/)

## Next

[Section titled “Next”](#next)

[Call a candidate](calls/call-a-candidate/)Start a call from Paladin so it's transcribed, analyzed, and filed on the record.

[Glossary](reference/glossary/)What Paladin means by a job, an opportunity, a General Call, and more.

# After the call

> Read the summary and transcript of a finished call, check its outcome, and file it under the right job.

When you hang up, Paladin writes a summary of the call, usually within a minute or two. You end up with the summary, key points, action items, the full transcript and an outcome, all filed on the candidate’s record.

1. Select **Calls** in the top bar, then select the call. Its summary page opens. You can also open it from the candidate’s page: under **Call History**, select **View Summary**.
2. Read **Summary**, **Key Points** and **Action Items**. If the page says **Generating summary…**, wait a minute and reload the page.
3. To read the whole conversation, select **Transcript** at the bottom. It opens to show who said what.
4. Check the outcome next to the date. Paladin fills it in from what was said on the call.
5. To change the outcome or add notes, open the call in the Paladin Dialer on your phone: on the **Calls** tab, select the call. Under **Outcome**, choose one, add **Notes** if you like, then select **Save outcome**.
6. If a General Call turned out to be about a job, open that opportunity. Under **Sources**, choose the call from **Attach existing call**.

The outcomes are:

| Outcome                 | Means                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Scheduled next**      | The next step is booked.                                                  |
| **Forwarded to client** | You’re sending the candidate to the client.                               |
| **Callback requested**  | Someone needs to call back.                                               |
| **No answer**           | The call didn’t connect. Only you set this one; Paladin never guesses it. |
| **Rejected**            | The candidate isn’t moving forward.                                       |

Paladin never replaces an outcome you saved.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The call also shows on the candidate’s page under **Call History**, with the job it was about, or **General**. A call about a job shows on that opportunity’s page too, with your outcome notes.

A call you attach to an opportunity appears under **Sources**, in **Linked Paladin calls**, and Paladin reads it along with the other material there.

The summary page also has **Send working-style survey**, which builds a short survey from the call and emails it to the candidate.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“Generating summary…” doesn’t go away.** The page doesn’t update by itself. Reload it.
* **“Summary unavailable for this call.”** Writing the summary failed. Paladin tries again on its own, so check back later.
* **There’s no summary and the Calls list says “skipped.”** The call was too short to summarize, for example a quick hang-up.
* **The call says “Unknown caller.”** The number isn’t on any candidate. In **Calls**, select the person icon on that row (**Create candidate from this caller**). Enter a **First name**, then select **Create candidate**. Paladin names the caller’s record, and their calls stay on it.
* **Attach existing call isn’t there.** It appears only when the candidate has a call that isn’t already attached to this opportunity, and only if you can edit the opportunity.
* **You attached the call to the wrong job.** Under **Linked Paladin calls**, select the unlink icon on the call (**Detach from this opportunity**), then attach it to the right one.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The steps are the same.

# Call a candidate

> Start a call from a candidate's page so Paladin can transcribe it, show suggestions live, and file the summary on the record.

Start the call from the candidate’s page, and Paladin does the rest. It rings your phone, connects you to the candidate, shows the transcript and suggested questions while you talk, then writes the summary onto the candidate’s record.

Before you start

* The candidate needs a phone number on their record.
* Your phone needs to be set up in Paladin. See [Set up your account](../../get-started/set-up-your-account/).

1. Open **Candidates** and select the candidate.
2. Select **Call Candidate**.
3. Under **What is this call about?**, choose the job you’re calling about. Each job shows the candidate’s fit score and where they are in the process. If the call isn’t about one job, choose **General Call**.
4. Under **Call from**, check the phone next to **From**. That’s the phone Paladin rings for you. To use a different one, select the arrow next to the button and pick it under **Switch calling number**.
5. Select **Launch Call Console**. The Call Console opens in a new tab.
6. Your phone rings. Answer it, and Paladin calls the candidate and connects you. The candidate sees your Paladin number.

Caution

Calls are transcribed, and Paladin doesn’t announce that on the call yet. Tell the person you’re calling.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The status at the top of the **Intelligence** panel shows **Waiting for audio** until the candidate picks up, then **Live** while Paladin listens. See [Use the Call Console](../the-call-console/) for what each panel shows.

Hang up on your phone when you’re done. Closing the Call Console tab doesn’t end the call; it only stops showing it. After the call, the summary is filed on the candidate’s record, under the job you chose. See [After the call](../after-the-call/).

Tip

Away from your computer? You can also call from the [Paladin Dialer](../../dialer/place-a-call-from-your-phone/) app on your phone. Those calls are transcribed too.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The dialog says “No phone number configured.”** Select **Set Up Phone** and add your number, then try again.
* **You see “Candidate has no phone number on file.”** Add a phone number to the candidate’s record, then try again.
* **No new tab opens.** Your browser blocked it as a pop-up. Allow pop-ups for Paladin in your browser, then select **Launch Call Console** again.
* **Your phone never rings.** Check the number next to **From**. If it’s wrong, pick another under **Switch calling number**, or fix it in your **Profile**. Then select **Launch Call Console** again.
* **You see “Failed to start call. Check your phone settings.”** Open your **Profile** and check that your phone number is right, then try again.
* **The console stays on “Waiting for audio.”** The candidate hasn’t picked up yet, or you didn’t answer when your phone rang. Hang up and launch the call again.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The steps are the same.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Use the Call Console](../the-call-console/)
* [After the call](../after-the-call/)

# Find a past call

> Look up any call you've made or taken by name, number or outcome, and open its summary.

The **Calls** page lists every call you’ve made or taken, newest first. Search it to find one call and open its summary and transcript.

1. Select **Calls** in the top bar.
2. To narrow the list, type a name, part of a number, or an outcome in the search box.
3. Select the call. Its summary page opens.
4. If the call is older than the list goes, scroll to the bottom and select **Load 100 more**.

Each row shows the candidate, the number, the direction (**in** or **out**), when it happened, how long it lasted, the outcome and whether the summary is ready. Calls placed from the Paladin Dialer are marked **mobile**.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The summary page shows the summary, key points, action items and the full transcript. See [After the call](../../calls/after-the-call/).

A call that’s still going appears in a card above the list, marked **Call in progress**. Select it to watch the call live.

To see only one candidate’s calls, open the candidate’s page and look under **Call History**.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“No calls match” your search.** Search looks at candidate names, numbers and outcomes. Numbers match only as they’re stored, so try the last four digits. For an outcome, type one word, such as `scheduled` or `rejected`.
* **The page says “No calls yet.”** Calls show up here once you’ve made or taken one through Paladin. Calls made from your phone’s own dialer don’t go through Paladin.
* **The call shows “Unknown caller.”** The number isn’t on any candidate. To make one, see [After the call](../../calls/after-the-call/).

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [After the call](../../calls/after-the-call/)
* [Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/)

# Use the Call Console

> What each part of the Call Console shows during a call, from the live transcript to suggested questions, on a computer or a phone.

The Call Console shows a call while it happens: what’s being said, what Paladin makes of it, and the brief it prepared. You talk and hang up on your phone. The console has no buttons to dial or hang up, and closing it never ends the call.

Before you start

The console opens when you [call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/). If a call is already under way, select **Open Call Console** at the top of the web app.

1. Check the status at the top of the **Intelligence** panel. It shows **Waiting for audio** until the call connects, then **Live** once Paladin hears you talking.
2. Follow the conversation under **Live Transcript**. Each line shows who spoke and how far into the call it was.
3. Watch **Intelligence** for cards. Each card is one topic of the conversation: notes collect under its heading, and **Ask about** lists questions to ask next, newest on top.
4. To have Paladin explain what was just said, select **Explain that**. The answer appears as a card titled **You asked**.
5. On a call about a job, use **Script** for the opening, the questions and the close. Use **Gaps & Questions** for the gaps to probe and the questions you must ask, and tick them off as you go.
6. On a General Call, check **Details**. Names, numbers and dates collect there as they’re said.
7. Hang up on your phone when you’re done.

### Job call or General Call

[Section titled “Job call or General Call”](#job-call-or-general-call)

|              | Call about a job                                                                          | General Call                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left panel   | **Script** and **Gaps & Questions**, from the brief                                       | **Details**, filled in as you talk                                                             |
| Intelligence | Topic cards and suggested questions                                                       | Topic cards, plus **We said we’d** (what you promised) and **They want** (what they asked for) |
| Scores       | **Consistency**, **Specificity** and **Communication**, after the first couple of minutes | None                                                                                           |

The menu next to **Explain that** shows which kind of help is running: **recruiter** for a job call, **summary** for a General Call. You can switch it for this call, but a General Call has no brief for **Recruiter** to work from.

On a phone

On a narrow screen the console shows one panel at a time. Use the tabs at the top: **Intelligence**, **Transcript**, and **Prep** (**Details** on a General Call). The phone layout hides the status, the mode menu and **Explain that**. Use a computer for those.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

When both of you have hung up, the status shows **Call ended**. Paladin keeps listening for a few seconds to finish its notes, then shows **All analysis captured.** You can close the tab.

Paladin then writes the call summary. See [After the call](../../calls/after-the-call/).

To write a report for the client from this call, select **Generate Report** at the top. It opens in the web app. If the call is still going, Paladin asks first, because the transcript isn’t complete yet.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The status stays on “Waiting for audio.”** The call hasn’t connected yet. Answer your phone when it rings. If it never rang, close the tab and launch the call again from the candidate’s page.
* **Explain that is gray.** It works only while the call is on, and one question at a time. While Paladin is answering, the button reads **AI responding…**.
* **You see “Call intelligence is temporarily unavailable.”** The cards have paused. Keep talking; the transcript keeps running, and the summary after the call doesn’t depend on the cards.
* **Script and Gaps & Questions are empty.** The call was launched as a General Call, so there’s no brief. Next time, choose the job under **What is this call about?**

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The console works the same way.

* [Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/)

# Add a candidate

> Add one candidate from a LinkedIn URL, a résumé, or your notes, and Paladin builds their profile for you.

Give Paladin a LinkedIn URL, a résumé, or your notes, and it creates the candidate right away, then fills in their name, contact details and profile from what you gave it. You don’t have to type anything else.

1. Open **Candidates** and select **Add Candidate**.

2. Give Paladin at least one source. Any one is enough, and more is better:

   * **LinkedIn URL**: the full profile address, in the form linkedin.com/in/…
   * A résumé: drag it onto **Drag a resume here or click to browse**, or select the box to pick a file. PDF, DOCX, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB each. You can add more than one file.
   * **Recruiter notes**: how you met, who referred them, why they’re a fit.

3. Leave **Name**, **Email** and **Phone** empty unless you want to set them yourself. Paladin fills them in from your sources, and anything you type wins. If you have no source, type a **Name** (a first name is enough).

4. Optional: choose **How did this candidate come to you?**

5. Leave **Visible to all recruiters** on to share the candidate with your team. Turn it off to keep a private draft that only you can see.

6. Select **Build profile & save**. If you added only a name, the button says **Save**.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The candidate appears at the top of your **Candidates** list straight away, with **(building)** after their name. Until Paladin finds the real name, it shows a stand-in: a name from the LinkedIn address, the file name, or “New candidate”.

You can open the candidate while it builds. Their page shows **Building profile…** and updates by itself when the build is done. When it finishes, the real name, contact details and profile replace the stand-in, and the candidate’s status changes to **New**.

If you saved with a name only, there’s nothing to build. The candidate is saved as **New** and you can add a résumé later from their page.

Next, [add the candidate to a job](../add-a-candidate-to-a-job/) to get a fit score and a call script.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The save button is gray and says “Add a LinkedIn, a resume, or a name.”** Paladin needs at least one of those. Add a source or type a name.
* **“… exceeds 10 MB limit.”** The file is too big. Save a smaller copy, for example a PDF without large images, and add it again.
* **“… has unsupported type.”** Use a PDF, a Word file (.docx), or a photo (JPG or PNG). Older Word files (.doc) don’t work: save them as .docx or PDF first.
* **“Save failed: …”** Nothing was created. Select the button again. If it keeps failing, use the feedback link at the bottom of this page.
* **The candidate page says “Profile build failed”.** Select **Retry**. Paladin already has your files and LinkedIn URL, so you don’t need to add them again.
* **The progress shows “LinkedIn lookup failed”.** Check the LinkedIn URL on the candidate’s page. It must be the full profile address (linkedin.com/in/…), not a search result or a company page.
* **The build finished but the name is still the stand-in.** Paladin couldn’t find a name in your sources, for example because the résumé is a photo or the LinkedIn profile is private. Select the name at the top of the candidate’s page and type the right one.

# Add a candidate to a job

> Put a candidate on a job so Paladin scores their fit and writes a call script for that job.

Add a candidate to a job and Paladin creates an opportunity: it compares the candidate with the job, gives a fit score, and writes a call script and questions for that job. You can start from the candidate or from the job.

Before you start

You can add a candidate to a job if the candidate is yours, or if you’re an admin.

1. Open **Candidates** and select the candidate.
2. Under **Opportunities**, select **Add Opportunity**.
3. Find the job under **Search jobs by title** and select it.
4. Leave **Generate fitment analysis and call script immediately** checked.
5. Select **Add & Analyze**.

On the **Candidates** list you can do the same from a candidate’s row: select the plus icon (**Add Job**).

### From the job’s page

[Section titled “From the job’s page”](#from-the-jobs-page)

1. Open **Jobs** and select the job.
2. Under **Opportunities**, select **Add Candidate**. This adds someone who is already in Paladin; it doesn’t create a new candidate.
3. Find the person under **Search candidates by name** and select them.
4. Leave **Auto-analyze after adding** checked, then select **Add**.

### Let Paladin suggest candidates

[Section titled “Let Paladin suggest candidates”](#let-paladin-suggest-candidates)

The job’s page has a **Who to research** list that ranks candidates against what the job asks for.

1. On the job’s page, under **Who to research**, select **Find candidates** (or **Refresh** if it has run before). Paladin decides what a strong match looks like, shown as chips marked **must have**, **strong** or **nice to have**, and ranks candidates against them.
2. Check the candidates you want. Someone marked **misses a must-have** is missing at least one must-have.
3. Select **Add** (the button shows how many) to add them to the job. Each one is analyzed.

The percentage in this list only ranks candidates against the chips. The fit score comes from the full analysis after you add them.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The steps are the same.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The job appears in the candidate’s **Opportunities** list (and the candidate in the job’s) with a **Fit Score** and a **Status**:

* **analyzing**: Paladin is working on it. The fit score shows **–** until it’s done.
* **ready**: the fit score and analysis are done. Select the row to [read the fit analysis](../read-the-fit-analysis/).
* **new**: you unchecked the analysis option, so nothing has run yet. Select the **Analyze** icon on the row, or open the opportunity and select **Analyze**.
* **error**: the analysis couldn’t run. A line under the row says why, with a button that fixes it (see below).

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“… has no resume or LinkedIn.”** Select **Add resume or LinkedIn** and add one on the candidate’s page. The analysis runs by itself once their profile is built.
* **“… hasn’t been researched yet.”** about the candidate: select **Research candidate**. The analysis runs again by itself when that’s done.
* **“The … job hasn’t been researched yet.”** Select **Research job**. The analysis runs when the job research finishes.
* **“… profile is still being built. The analysis will run when it finishes.”** Nothing to do. Wait for the candidate’s profile to finish.
* **“The analysis didn’t finish. Press Analyze to try again.”** Open the opportunity and select **Analyze**.
* **The dialog stays open after you select Add & Analyze.** The candidate is probably on that job already. Each candidate can be on each job once. Close the dialog and check the **Opportunities** list.
* **There’s no Add Opportunity button.** The candidate belongs to another recruiter. Ask them or an admin to add the job.
* **Who to research says “… can’t be matched yet”.** Open the list to see the reason for each person. Often their profile hasn’t been built yet.
* **Who to research says “… not read yet. Press Refresh.”** Select **Refresh**.

## Related

# Read the fit analysis

> Find a candidate's fit score for a job, see what's behind it, prepare for the call, and change the score if you disagree.

Each time you add a candidate to a job, Paladin writes a fit analysis: a fit score, the candidate’s strengths and gaps for that job, and a call script with the questions to ask. It’s all on the opportunity’s page.

Before you start

The candidate needs to be on the job. See [Add a candidate to a job](../add-a-candidate-to-a-job/).

1. Open the candidate and, under **Opportunities**, select the job. You can also get there from the job’s **Opportunities** list, or from **Opportunities** in the menu.

2. Read **At a glance** first. It has the fit score, a one-line verdict, the **Top strengths** and **Top gaps**, and when you last called. If the job’s notes list must-haves, **Job note requirements** marks each one **Met**, **Not met** or **Verify on call**.

3. For the reasoning, open **Fitment Analysis**:

   * **Strengths**: what the candidate brings, the evidence, and why it matters for this job.
   * **Gaps**: what’s missing, marked **low**, **medium** or **high**, with how to address it.
   * **Red Flags**: anything that doesn’t add up, each with a **Probe:** question to ask about it.
   * **Culture Fit**: notes on how they’d fit the team.

4. Before you call, read **Call Script**: an **Opening**, timed sections of questions, and a **Close** with **Selling points:** for the job. Then check **Quick Reference**: **Must Ask**, **Should Ask**, **If Time Permits**, and what to ask **If Concerned**.

5. To change the fit score, type a number from 0 to 100 in the **Fit Score** box, then press Enter or click outside the box. Paladin shows its own score next to yours, as **AI: …%**.

6. To run the analysis again, select **Re-Analyze**.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The score you type is kept. When the analysis runs again, Paladin updates its own score but doesn’t change yours. To hand the score back to Paladin, clear the box and press Enter.

**Re-Analyze** takes a moment, and the page shows its progress while it works. To stop it, select **Cancel analysis**; the previous analysis stays.

When something new lands after the analysis, such as a note or a document, a banner says **New context since last analysis**, with a **Re-analyze** button. The analysis doesn’t re-run on its own.

When you [call the candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/) about this job, the Call Console shows your brief for the call under **Script** and **Prep**.

A fit score of 75% or more shows in green, 50% to 74% in yellow, and below 50% in red.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **There’s no analysis, just a message and a button.** The analysis couldn’t run yet. The message says why; select the button next to it (**Add resume or LinkedIn**, **Research candidate** or **Research job**). See [Add a candidate to a job](../add-a-candidate-to-a-job/#if-something-goes-wrong).
* **“Fit score must be between 0 and 100”.** Type a whole number from 0 to 100.
* **“Couldn’t cancel the analysis. Try again.”** Select **Cancel analysis** again.
* **You can’t type in the Fit Score box.** The candidate belongs to another recruiter. You can read the analysis, but only the owner or an admin can change the score or run the analysis again.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. Everything else is the same.

# Upload many résumés

> Upload a batch of résumés or a whole folder at once, and Paladin creates a candidate from each one.

Upload a batch of résumés, or a whole folder, in one go. Paladin reads each one and creates a candidate, or adds the résumé to a candidate you already have with the same email or phone. You get an import page that shows what happened to every file.

1. Open **Candidates** and select **Bulk upload**.
2. Drop résumés or a folder onto the box, or select **Choose files** or **Choose a folder**. PDF, Word (.docx), text or photos, up to 10 MB each.
3. Check the count that says how many files are ready. Files that aren’t résumés, such as spreadsheets and system files, are skipped for you.
4. Select **Upload** (the button shows how many résumés). Keep the window open until the upload finishes.
5. When the upload is done, select **View import**.
6. Select **Needs attention** to see only the rows you need to look at. Select a row to open it and fix it (see below).

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

Paladin reads the résumés one by one. The upload window gives you an estimate of how long it takes. You don’t need to wait: the import page keeps going while you’re away and shows **Reading resumes: … done.** while it works. When everything is read and nothing needs you, it says **Every resume is in. Nothing needs your attention.**

Each row ends up with one of these statuses:

* **Imported**: a new candidate was created.
* **Added to existing**: the résumé has the same email or phone as a candidate you already have, so Paladin added it to that candidate’s record instead of creating a duplicate.
* **Needs review**: Paladin couldn’t find a name. Nothing is created until you add one.
* **Failed**: the file couldn’t be read. The row says why and what to do.

Candidates created this way are visible to all recruiters. To get back to an import later, open **Candidates**, select **Imports**, then the import.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

Open a row to see its full message and the actions for it.

* **“No name found in this file. Add the candidate’s name to import them.”** Enter the **First name** (and anything else you know), then select **Import candidate**. To see the résumé, select **Open the original file**.
* **“Only a first name was found.” or “No email or phone found.”** The candidate was created. Add what’s missing and select **Save**, or select **Mark reviewed** if it’s fine as it is.
* **“… is already a candidate, with different contact details. Check it isn’t the same person.”** Select **Open candidate** and compare it with the candidate you already had. If it’s the same person, open the extra candidate’s page and select **Archive**.
* **Paladin added the résumé to the wrong person (“Same email as …”).** Open the row and select **Different person: create new**.
* **“Paladin couldn’t read this file” or “couldn’t make a profile from it”.** Select **Read again**. If it still fails, add this candidate by hand with [Add a candidate](../add-a-candidate/).
* **“Older Word (.doc) files can’t be read.”** (or RTF, Pages, OpenDocument) Save the file as .docx or PDF, then select **Upload more** on the import page and add it.
* **“The file is … MB; the limit is 10 MB.”** Save a smaller copy and add it with **Upload more**.
* **“… didn’t reach the server (connection problem).”** Select **Upload more** on the import page and add those files again.
* **“Couldn’t start the upload. Check your connection and try again.”** Nothing was uploaded. Check your connection and select **Upload** again.
* **You want the failed rows gone.** Select **Remove failed** on the import page.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Add a candidate](../add-a-candidate/)
* [Add a candidate to a job](../add-a-candidate-to-a-job/)

# Change Dialer settings

> Check which account the Paladin Dialer is connected to, choose which of your phones Paladin rings, or disconnect the app.

Settings is the gear at the top right of the **Calls**, **Contacts** and **Keypad** tabs. It shows the account the app is connected to, and lets you choose which phone Paladin rings or disconnect the app.

## Choose which phone Paladin rings

[Section titled “Choose which phone Paladin rings”](#choose-which-phone-paladin-rings)

When a candidate calls your Paladin number, Paladin rings one of the phones on your account.

1. Tap the gear at the top right.
2. Under **Phone Paladin rings**, tap the phone you want. A check mark moves to it.
3. Tap **Done**.

To add or remove a phone, use **Phone Numbers** in your **Profile** in the dashboard. The app can only switch between the phones already there.

## Disconnect the app, or switch accounts

[Section titled “Disconnect the app, or switch accounts”](#disconnect-the-app-or-switch-accounts)

1. Tap the gear at the top right.
2. Tap **Disconnect this device**. It disconnects at once, without asking first.
3. To connect again, with the same account or another one, follow [Connect the Dialer to your account](../pair-the-dialer/).

Disconnecting clears the account’s calls, candidates and favorites from the phone. Your phone’s own contacts aren’t touched.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

Settings shows **Connected**, your name, your Paladin number, and **Connected to** with your dashboard address. To change the dashboard address or your login, disconnect and connect again.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“Sign-in expired.”** You changed your dashboard password. Disconnect the app and connect again with the new password.
* **“Couldn’t load your phones.”** Check your connection, tap **Done**, and open Settings again.
* **“No phones on your account.”** Add your phone under **Phone Numbers** in your **Profile** in the dashboard.
* **“Couldn’t switch phones.”** Check your connection and tap the phone again.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Connect the Dialer to your account](../pair-the-dialer/)
* [Set up your account](../../get-started/set-up-your-account/)
* [Fix Dialer problems](../dialer-troubleshooting/)

# Fix Dialer problems

> What to do when the Paladin Dialer won't connect, a call doesn't go through or isn't transcribed, or your contacts don't show.

Find the message or problem you see below. Most Dialer problems come from one of three things: the app isn’t connected, the phone isn’t on your account, or the call was placed from outside the app.

## Connecting

[Section titled “Connecting”](#connecting)

* **“Sign-in failed.”** The dashboard address, email or password is wrong. Check that they work in your browser. The address is the one you sign in to Paladin at; pasting the whole address from your browser is fine.
* **“Your account has no phone number assigned.”** Ask your Paladin admin to assign you a Paladin number.
* **“This account can’t get a PIN automatically.”** Ask your Paladin admin for your PIN, enter it, and tap **Connect**.
* **“Sign-in expired.”** (a red bar on **Calls** or **Contacts**). Your dashboard password changed. Tap the gear, tap **Disconnect this device**, and connect again with the new password.

## Calls

[Section titled “Calls”](#calls)

* **The call doesn’t reach the person.** This phone needs to be one of the phones under **Phone Numbers** in your **Profile** in the dashboard. Add its number there.
* **The call isn’t in Paladin, or isn’t transcribed.** It was placed from your phone’s own dialer, Contacts app or call log. Always start work calls from the Paladin Dialer.
* **“Invalid number.”** The Dialer calls US numbers only: 10 digits, or 11 starting with 1.
* **“Could not start the call.”** Your phone didn’t accept the call from the app. Try again. On Android, check that Paladin Dialer is allowed to make phone calls in your phone’s settings.
* **On Android, the Phone app opens with the call ready, but doesn’t call.** You didn’t allow Paladin Dialer to make phone calls. Tap call in the Phone app, or allow the permission in your phone’s settings.
* **The Call in progress bar doesn’t appear.** It takes about 15 seconds. Switch away from the app and back. See [See a call live on your phone](../see-a-call-live-on-your-phone/).

## Contacts

[Section titled “Contacts”](#contacts)

* **“Phone contacts are off.”** You didn’t allow access to your contacts. Candidates and teammates still show. To see your phone’s contacts too, allow Paladin Dialer to access Contacts in your phone’s settings.
* **Only some of your phone’s contacts show (iPhone).** You gave the app access to selected contacts only. In your iPhone’s settings, give Paladin Dialer full access to Contacts.
* **“No contacts yet.”** Tap **Reload contacts**.
* **“Offline.”** (a bar at the top). The app can’t reach Paladin, so it shows what it saved last time. Check your connection; the bar goes away when the app reconnects.

## Installing

[Section titled “Installing”](#installing)

* **The TestFlight invitation doesn’t arrive (iPhone).** Check spam. Check that the email you gave us is the one your Apple ID uses.
* **Android says the app isn’t installed.** Uninstall the older Paladin Dialer from before September 2026, then install again.

If none of this helps, use the feedback link at the bottom of this page.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Install the Paladin Dialer](../install-the-dialer/)
* [Connect the Dialer to your account](../pair-the-dialer/)
* [Change Dialer settings](../dialer-settings/)

# Install the Paladin Dialer

> Put the Paladin Dialer on your iPhone (through TestFlight) or Android phone (from a download), so the calls you make from your phone run through Paladin.

The Paladin Dialer is the app you call candidates from on your phone. Calls you place from it run through Paladin, so they’re transcribed and filed in your dashboard. Installing takes a few minutes. The full install page, with the Android download button, is at [paladinrecruiter.com/dialer](https://paladinrecruiter.com/dialer).

Before you start

You need your Paladin account set up, with your cell phone’s number on it. See [Set up your account](../../get-started/set-up-your-account/).

## iPhone

[Section titled “iPhone”](#iphone)

The iPhone app installs through **TestFlight**, Apple’s own app for apps on their way to the App Store.

1. Install **TestFlight** from the App Store. It’s free and made by Apple.
2. Send us the email address your Apple ID uses. We send you an invitation.
3. Open the invitation, tap **Accept**, then **Install**.

## Android

[Section titled “Android”](#android)

1. On your phone, open [paladinrecruiter.com/dialer](https://paladinrecruiter.com/dialer) and tap **Download for Android**. Then open the downloaded file.
2. If Android asks, allow installs from your browser, then go back.
3. Tap **Install**, then **Open**.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The app opens on the **Calls** tab and asks you to connect it to your account. Continue with [Connect the Dialer to your account](../pair-the-dialer/).

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The TestFlight invitation doesn’t arrive.** It comes from “Ashford and Briggs LLC via TestFlight”. Check your spam folder. If it isn’t there, check that the email you sent us is the one your Apple ID uses.
* **TestFlight can’t install the app.** TestFlight is signed in with a different Apple ID from the one we invited. Sign in to TestFlight with the invited Apple ID.
* **Android says the app isn’t installed.** You have an older Paladin Dialer on the phone from before September 2026. Uninstall it, then open the downloaded file again.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Connect the Dialer to your account](../pair-the-dialer/)
* [Fix Dialer problems](../dialer-troubleshooting/)
* [Install page](https://paladinrecruiter.com/dialer)

# Connect the Dialer to your account

> Sign in to the Paladin Dialer with your dashboard address, email and password, and allow the permissions it asks for.

Connect the app once, with the same login you use for Paladin in your browser. After that, every call you place from the app goes out through your Paladin number.

Before you start

* Your account needs a Paladin number. Open your **Profile** in Paladin: if it says **Not assigned**, ask your Paladin admin to assign one.
* The phone you’re setting up must be one of your **Phone Numbers** in your **Profile**.

1. Open **Paladin Dialer**. On the **Calls** tab, tap **Connect now**. (Or tap the gear at the top right.)
2. Under **Connect to Paladin Recruiter**, enter your **Dashboard address**: the address you sign in to Paladin at in your browser. You can paste the whole address from your browser; the app keeps only the part it needs.
3. Enter your **Email** and **Password**, the same ones you use for the dashboard. Your phone’s password manager can fill them in.
4. Tap **Connect**. The app signs you in and takes you back to your calls.
5. Open the **Contacts** tab. When your phone asks for access to your contacts, allow it.
6. On Android only: the first time you place a call, Android asks to let Paladin Dialer make and manage phone calls. Allow it.

## What the app asks for, and why

[Section titled “What the app asks for, and why”](#what-the-app-asks-for-and-why)

* **Contacts** (iPhone and Android). The app lists your phone’s contacts next to your candidates and teammates so you can call them through Paladin. On iPhone the prompt says “Paladin Dialer shows your contacts so you can call them through Paladin.” Your contacts stay on the phone; they’re never uploaded.
* **Phone calls** (Android only). Lets the app place the call for you with one tap. If you don’t allow it, the app opens your phone’s dialer with the number filled in, and you tap call yourself.

The app doesn’t ask for your microphone or for notifications. The call itself runs in your phone’s own Phone app.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

To check which account the phone is on, tap the gear. It shows **Connected**, your name, your Paladin number, and the dashboard address.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“Sign-in failed.”** The dashboard address, email or password is wrong. Check that you can sign in with them in your browser, then try again.
* **“Your account has no phone number assigned.”** Ask your Paladin admin to assign you a Paladin number, then tap **Connect** again.
* **“This account can’t get a PIN automatically.”** A PIN field appears. Ask your Paladin admin for your PIN, enter it, and tap **Connect**.
* **“Enter your dashboard address, email, and password.”** One of the fields is empty.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Place a call from your phone](../place-a-call-from-your-phone/)
* [Change Dialer settings](../dialer-settings/)
* [Fix Dialer problems](../dialer-troubleshooting/)

# Place a call from your phone

> Call a candidate, teammate or contact from the Paladin Dialer so the call runs through Paladin, shows your Paladin number, and is transcribed.

Tap a name or number in the Paladin Dialer and the app places the call through Paladin. The person you call sees your Paladin number, and Paladin transcribes the call and files it in your dashboard.

Before you start

The app must be [connected to your account](../pair-the-dialer/).

1. Open **Paladin Dialer** and choose where to call from:

   * **Contacts**: type a name or number under **Search people and numbers**, then tap the person. Each row shows where it comes from: **Candidate**, **Team**, or **Phone** (your phone’s contacts).
   * **Calls**: tap the phone icon next to a past call.
   * **Keypad**: enter the number, then tap **Call via Paladin**.

2. Your phone’s Phone app takes over. On iPhone, confirm the call when iPhone asks. On Android the call starts on its own.

3. Wait a few seconds while Paladin connects the call. You may hear tones before it rings through.

4. Talk as usual. Hang up in the Phone app when you’re done.

Caution

Calls are transcribed, and Paladin doesn’t announce that on the call yet. Tell the person you’re calling.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

About 15 seconds into the call, a bar appears at the bottom of the app: **Call in progress**. Tap it to follow the call live. See [See a call live on your phone](../see-a-call-live-on-your-phone/).

The call shows at the top of **Calls** right away. In the dashboard’s **Calls** list, calls from the Dialer are marked **mobile**. If the number belongs to a candidate in Paladin, the call is filed on their record.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“Invalid number.”** The Dialer only calls US numbers. Check that the number has 10 digits, or 11 starting with 1.
* **“No number on file for this contact.”** Tap the info icon next to the contact to check their numbers, or add one to the candidate in Paladin.
* **The call doesn’t reach the person.** This phone needs to be one of the phones under **Phone Numbers** in your **Profile**. Add its number there, then call again.
* **The call isn’t transcribed.** It was placed from your phone’s own dialer or Contacts app instead of the Paladin Dialer. Hang up and call again from the Paladin Dialer.

More fixes: [Fix Dialer problems](../dialer-troubleshooting/).

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [See a call live on your phone](../see-a-call-live-on-your-phone/)
* [Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/) from the dashboard
* [Paladin number](../../reference/glossary/#paladin-number) in the glossary

# Review a call on your phone

> Read a call's summary and transcript in the Paladin Dialer, and record how the call went, right after you hang up.

Every call that went through Paladin is on the **Calls** tab. Open one to read the summary and transcript, and to record the outcome while it’s fresh. What you save here is saved in your dashboard too.

1. Open **Paladin Dialer**. It opens on **Calls**.
2. Tap the call. To find an older one, type a name or number under **Search Paladin calls**.
3. Read **Summary**, **Key points** and **Action items**. To read the whole conversation, tap **Transcript**.
4. Under **Outcome**, tap the one that fits: **Scheduled next**, **Forwarded to client**, **Callback requested**, **No answer** or **Rejected**.
5. Add anything worth remembering under **Notes**, then tap **Save outcome**. The button changes to **Saved**.
6. To see the candidate’s profile, jobs and documents, tap their name (**Profile, opportunities and documents**).

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The outcome shows under the call in your **Calls** list, here and in the dashboard. Reports made for the call are listed under **Reports**; tap one to read it.

If the caller isn’t a candidate in Paladin yet, you see **Name this caller** instead of their name. Type their name under **Full name**, or tap **Link to phone contact** to use the name from your phone’s contacts, then tap **Save name**.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **“No summary yet.”** The summary appears a minute or two after the call ends. Go back and open the call again.
* **“Couldn’t save the outcome.”** Check your connection and tap **Save outcome** again.
* **“Sign-in expired.”** Your dashboard password changed. Reconnect the app; see [Change Dialer settings](../dialer-settings/). Then save again.
* **Tapping a call dials it instead of opening it.** Paladin hasn’t registered the call yet. Wait a minute, pull down on **Calls** to refresh, then tap it again.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [See a call live on your phone](../see-a-call-live-on-your-phone/)
* [Place a call from your phone](../place-a-call-from-your-phone/)

# See a call live on your phone

> Open the Live Console in the Paladin Dialer during a call to read the transcript and the AI's suggestions on your phone.

While a call you placed from the Dialer is in progress, the app can show the Call Console: the live transcript and the AI’s suggestions, on the same phone. Viewing it doesn’t affect the call.

Before you start

The call must be one you [placed from the Paladin Dialer](../place-a-call-from-your-phone/), or a call to your Paladin number.

1. During the call, switch from your Phone app back to **Paladin Dialer**. Use speaker or headphones so you can talk while you look.
2. Tap the **Call in progress** bar at the bottom of the screen (**Open console**). You can also tap **Call in progress** at the top of the **Calls** tab.
3. The live console opens, titled **Live** and the number you called. It starts on **Intelligence**. Switch to **Transcript** or **Prep** with the tabs at the top.
4. To have Paladin explain the last thing that was said, tap **Explain that** on **Intelligence**.
5. Hang up in your Phone app when you’re done. The console has no hang-up button; leaving it doesn’t end the call.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

When the call ends, the bar goes away. The summary appears on the call a minute or two later: open **Calls** and tap the call. See [Review a call on your phone](../review-a-call-on-your-phone/).

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The Call in progress bar doesn’t appear.** Paladin takes about 15 seconds to register the call. Switch away from the app and back to check again. If it still doesn’t appear, the call didn’t go through Paladin, for example because it was placed from your phone’s own dialer.
* **“Couldn’t load the call console.”** Check your phone’s connection, go back, and tap the bar again.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Place a call from your phone](../place-a-call-from-your-phone/)
* [Use the Call Console](../../calls/the-call-console/)
* [Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/) from the dashboard

# Set up your account

> Your first sign-in to Paladin Recruiter. Set the phone that rings, your caller ID name, and your password. It takes about a minute.

The first time you sign in, Paladin asks for three things: the phone that should ring when candidates call you, the name candidates see on caller ID, and a password of your own. It takes about a minute.

Before you start

You need the email address and temporary password from your invite. Have your cell phone nearby.

1. Sign in with the email address and temporary password from your invite. The welcome screen opens. Select **Let’s go**.
2. Under **Your phone number**, enter the number of the phone you want to ring when candidates call you, usually your cell. If it isn’t a US number, choose the country code first. Select **Next**.
3. Under **How candidates see you**, check your **Display name (caller ID)**. This is the name candidates see when you call them, and the name Paladin uses for you in call scripts. Check that your **Timezone** is right, then select **Next**.
4. Under **Set your password**, enter a new password of at least 8 characters, then enter it again under **Confirm password**. Select **Next**.
5. Check the summary, then select **Start recruiting**.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

Paladin opens your **Home** page. From now on, when someone calls your Paladin number, your phone rings. You don’t need a desk phone or a plugin.

You can change any of these settings later in your **Profile**.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The Next button stays gray.** Something on that step is missing. You need a phone number on step 1 and a display name on step 2. On the password step, the password must be at least 8 characters and both entries must match. If they don’t, you’ll see **Passwords don’t match**.
* **Your temporary password doesn’t work.** Ask the person who sent your invite for a new one.
* **You get an error when you select Start recruiting.** Your answers are still there. Select **Back** to check each step, then try again. If it keeps failing, use the feedback link at the bottom of this page.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/)
* [Install the Paladin Dialer](../../dialer/install-the-dialer/) on your phone

# The recruiting workflow

> How a role moves through Paladin Recruiter, from a new job to a report in the hiring manager's inbox, with a link to each step.

Every role follows the same loop: set up the job, bring in candidates, screen them on the phone, and send the best ones to the hiring manager. Paladin does the research and the write-ups along the way. Each step below links to its own page.

## 1. Set up the job

[Section titled “1. Set up the job”](#1-set-up-the-job)

**[Create a job](../../jobs/create-a-job/)** with the title, the client, and the job description or posting link. Select **Research & Process** and Paladin researches the role and the company and builds the job profile it uses to judge candidates.

Then **[add the hiring manager](../../jobs/add-a-hiring-manager/)**: the person who will receive your reports.

## 2. Bring in candidates

[Section titled “2. Bring in candidates”](#2-bring-in-candidates)

**[Add a candidate](../../candidates/add-a-candidate/)** from a résumé, a LinkedIn link, or your notes, and Paladin builds their profile. Have a stack of résumés? **[Upload many résumés](../../candidates/upload-many-resumes/)** at once.

## 3. Match candidates to the job

[Section titled “3. Match candidates to the job”](#3-match-candidates-to-the-job)

**[Add a candidate to a job](../../candidates/add-a-candidate-to-a-job/)**, or let Paladin suggest who to look at from the job’s page. For each pairing, Paladin scores the fit and writes an analysis: strengths, gaps, red flags, and a call script. **[Read the fit analysis](../../candidates/read-the-fit-analysis/)** before you call.

## 4. Screen on the phone

[Section titled “4. Screen on the phone”](#4-screen-on-the-phone)

**[Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/)** from their page. Paladin rings your phone and connects you. While you talk, **[the Call Console](../../calls/the-call-console/)** shows the transcript and suggests questions. Away from your desk, use the **[Paladin Dialer](../../dialer/place-a-call-from-your-phone/)** on your phone.

## 5. Review the call

[Section titled “5. Review the call”](#5-review-the-call)

A few moments after you hang up, the summary, key points, and action items are on the candidate’s record. See **[After the call](../../calls/after-the-call/)**, and **[Find a past call](../../calls/find-a-past-call/)** when you need one later.

## 6. Report to the hiring manager

[Section titled “6. Report to the hiring manager”](#6-report-to-the-hiring-manager)

**[Create a candidate report](../../reports/create-a-candidate-report/)** from the call or from everything on file, set your verdict, and edit it until it reads right. Then **[send it to the hiring manager](../../reports/send-a-report/)**.

## 7. Keep the pipeline current

[Section titled “7. Keep the pipeline current”](#7-keep-the-pipeline-current)

**[Move the candidate along](../../pipeline/move-a-candidate-along/)** as things progress, and **[archive candidates](../../pipeline/archive-a-candidate/)** you’re done with so your lists stay short. Archiving can be undone.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs and **Divisions** instead of clients. The workflow is the same.

# Add a hiring manager

> Create a hiring manager from a job's page and link them to the job, so you can keep their contact details in one place and send them candidate reports.

Add the hiring manager from the job they’re hiring for. Paladin creates a contact record and links it to the job. One hiring manager can own several jobs, and you send them candidate reports from their page.

1. Open **Jobs** and select the job.
2. Scroll to the **Hiring manager** card and select **Link / Create**.
3. Search by name, title, email, or company. If the hiring manager is already in Paladin, select them. You’re done.
4. If they aren’t, select **Create new hiring manager**.
5. Enter their **Name**. Add their **Title**, **Email**, and **Phone** if you have them. **Company** is filled in from the job; change it if it’s wrong.
6. Select **Save**.

You can also add a hiring manager without a job: open **Hiring Managers** and select **Add Hiring Manager**. Link them to a job later from the job’s **Hiring manager** card.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The **Hiring manager** card on the job shows their name and contact details. Select the name to open their page. To link someone else, select **Change**. To remove the link, select **Unlink**.

The hiring manager’s page lists their contact details, their jobs, the calls on those jobs, documents, and notes. Any recruiter can edit the contact details: select a value to change it.

To send them a candidate report, open their page and select **Send report**, then choose the report. Paladin downloads the report and opens a draft email to them in your email app. Attach the downloaded report and send it.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The Save button stays gray.** The hiring manager needs a **Name**.
* **Send report is gray.** It needs two things: an email address on the hiring manager’s page, and at least one candidate report on one of their jobs. Add their email under **Contact**. The list only includes reports from your own calls, unless you’re an admin.
* **The card shows a name and a Convert to record button.** Someone typed the hiring manager’s details on this job before hiring managers were records. Select **Convert to record** to turn them into one.
* **The same person shows up twice in Hiring Managers.** Search before you create, and link the existing one.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Create a job](../create-a-job/)
* [Glossary](../../reference/glossary/)

# Create a job

> Add a job to Paladin from the Jobs page, give it a job description, and let Paladin research the role so it can match and screen candidates.

Add the job from the **Jobs** page. Give it a title and a job description, and Paladin researches the role. You end up with a job page that call scripts, fit scores, and candidate matching all work from.

Before you start

Have the job description handy, as a file or as text you can paste. A link to the public posting helps too.

1. Open **Jobs** and select **Add Job**.
2. Enter the **Title**, for example “Diesel Mechanic”.
3. Under **Job Provider (Company)**, choose the client the job is for. If they aren’t in the list, choose **+ Add New Provider**, enter their **Name**, and select **Save**.
4. If the job is posted online, paste the link into **Job Post URL**.
5. Add the job description. Drag the file into the box, or click the box to pick a file. You can also paste the text into **Paste job description**.
6. Select **Research & Process**.

To add the job without starting research, select **Add** instead of **Research & Process**. You can start research later from the job’s page with **Research Job**.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The job’s page opens and the research starts. A progress panel shows what Paladin is doing, under **Agent Activity**. You can stay and watch or come back later. When it’s done, the page shows the research, including the **Job Analysis**.

If you attached a file, it appears under **Documents** on the job’s page. Paladin reads it in the background.

The job starts as **active** and shows on your **Jobs** page and on **Home**, because you created it, so you own it. You can edit the title, description, and other details on the job’s page: select a value to change it.

Next steps:

* Link the job’s hiring manager, so you can send them candidate reports. See [Add a hiring manager](../add-a-hiring-manager/).
* To have Paladin suggest candidates from your database, scroll to **Who to research** and select **Find candidates**.
* When the job is on hold, filled, or closed, select the status next to the job’s title and choose the new one.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The Add and Research & Process buttons stay gray.** The job needs a **Title**. Enter one.
* **A message says the file “exceeds 10 MB limit.”** Use a smaller file, or paste the text into **Paste job description** instead.
* **A message says the file “has unsupported type.”** Paladin reads PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV, MD, HTML, JPG, and PNG files. Save the description in one of those formats, or paste the text.
* **You can’t find the job on the Jobs page.** You may be looking at another recruiter’s job. Tick **Show all jobs** to see everyone’s.
* **The research shows something wrong about the job.** Fix the job description or add a note on the job’s page, then select **Re-Research Job**.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs and **Division** instead of job provider. The steps are the same.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Add a hiring manager](../add-a-hiring-manager/)
* [Call a candidate](../../calls/call-a-candidate/)
* [Glossary](../../reference/glossary/)

# Archive a candidate

> Hide a candidate from your lists and from matching without losing their calls, texts, documents or opportunities, and restore them any time.

Archive a candidate you’re done with. They disappear from candidate lists, your Home tab and matching, but nothing is deleted. Their calls, texts, documents and opportunities stay, and you can restore them any time.

Before you start

The candidate must be yours, or you must be an admin.

1. Open **Candidates** and select the candidate.
2. At the top of the page, select **Archive**.
3. Confirm. You see “Candidate archived”.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The candidate’s page now shows “Archived by” with your name and the date, and the **Archive** button becomes **Restore**. The candidate no longer shows in the **Candidates** list, on your **Home** tab, or when Paladin looks for matching candidates for a job.

If an archived candidate calls or texts you, Paladin still matches them to their record. They stay archived.

## Find and restore an archived candidate

[Section titled “Find and restore an archived candidate”](#find-and-restore-an-archived-candidate)

1. Open **Candidates**.
2. Under **Status**, choose **Archived**. The newest archived are at the top.
3. Select **Restore** on the candidate’s row, or open the candidate and select **Restore**.

The candidate comes back exactly as they were. To go back to the full list, select **Show all candidates**.

Note

There is no delete button for candidates. Archiving is how you take someone out of view, because deleting would also remove the calls and history other recruiters may rely on.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **There’s no Archive button.** The candidate belongs to another recruiter. Ask them or an admin to archive it.
* **You see “Could not archive the candidate” or “Could not restore the candidate”.** Nothing changed. Refresh the page and try again.

## Related

[Section titled “Related”](#related)

* [Move a candidate along](../move-a-candidate-along/)
* [Glossary](../../reference/glossary/)

# Move a candidate along

> Change an opportunity's status as a candidate moves through the process for a job, or change the candidate's overall status.

Each opportunity (one candidate for one job) has a status. Change it on the opportunity page so everyone can see where the candidate stands for that job.

Before you start

The candidate must be yours, or you must be an admin. Otherwise the status shows but you can’t change it.

1. Open **Candidates** and select the candidate.
2. Under **Opportunities**, select the job. The opportunity page opens.
3. At the top, next to the candidate and job names, select the status.
4. Choose the new status: **new**, **ready**, **scheduled**, **in call**, **completed** or **rejected**.

The change saves straight away. You can also open the opportunity from **Opportunities** in the menu.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The new status shows on the opportunity page, on the candidate’s page and in the **Opportunities** list.

Paladin also sets some statuses itself. For example, it shows **analyzing** while it scores the candidate against the job, and **error** if the analysis can’t finish.

## The candidate’s own status

[Section titled “The candidate’s own status”](#the-candidates-own-status)

A candidate also has one overall status, separate from their opportunities. It sits at the top of the candidate’s page, next to **Call Candidate**. Select it to choose **New**, **Ready for Call**, **In Progress**, **Completed** or **Rejected**. Use the **Status** filter on the **Candidates** list to find candidates by it.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The status is plain text, not a menu.** The candidate belongs to another recruiter. Ask them or an admin to change it.
* **You see “Failed to update this opportunity”.** The change didn’t save and the old status is back. Refresh the page and try again.
* **The Opportunities list filter has no option for rejected.** The filter doesn’t offer every status. Choose **All** and look at the **Status** column.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The steps are the same.

# Glossary

> What Paladin Recruiter means by a job, an opportunity, a General Call, the Call Console, and other terms you'll see in the app.

### Brief

[Section titled “Brief”](#brief)

What Paladin prepares before a call from everything on file: résumé, LinkedIn, notes, and the job description. It appears in the Call Console under **Prep** and **Script**.

### Call Console

[Section titled “Call Console”](#call-console)

The screen that opens in a new tab when you launch a call. It shows the live transcript and the AI’s suggestions.

### Display name (caller ID)

[Section titled “Display name (caller ID)”](#display-name-caller-id)

The name candidates see when you call them. Change it in your **Profile**.

### Fit score

[Section titled “Fit score”](#fit-score)

A percentage showing how well a candidate matches a job’s requirements, based on everything on file.

### General Call

[Section titled “General Call”](#general-call)

A call that isn’t about one specific job. Paladin still transcribes it and writes a summary.

### Hiring manager

[Section titled “Hiring manager”](#hiring-manager)

The person at the client (or in your company) who owns a job and receives your candidate reports.

### Job (or **Role**)

[Section titled “Job (or Role)”](#job-or-role)

A position you’re recruiting for. Teams that recruit for their own company see **Roles** instead of jobs.

### Job provider (or **Division**)

[Section titled “Job provider (or Division)”](#job-provider-or-division)

The client company a job comes from. Teams that recruit for their own company see **Divisions**.

### Opportunity

[Section titled “Opportunity”](#opportunity)

One candidate being considered for one job. A candidate can have several opportunities, one for each job.

### Paladin Dialer

[Section titled “Paladin Dialer”](#paladin-dialer)

The phone app you use to place calls through Paladin. [Install it](../../dialer/install-the-dialer/).

### Paladin number

[Section titled “Paladin number”](#paladin-number)

Your business line. Calls to it ring your own phone, and calls you start from Paladin or the Paladin Dialer show it as the caller ID.

# Create a candidate report

> Generate a write-up of a candidate for one job from everything on file, pick its style, set your assessment, and edit it before you send it.

A candidate report is a short write-up of one candidate for one job, ready for the hiring manager. You don’t need a call first: Paladin builds it from whatever is on the opportunity, such as a phone screen transcript, notes, documents and call summaries.

Before you start

The candidate must be yours, or you must be an admin.

1. Open **Candidates** and select the candidate.
2. Under **Opportunities**, select the job you want the report for. The opportunity page opens.
3. Under **Reports**, select **Generate candidate report**. A dialog lists what the report will use.
4. Select **Generate report**. The report fills in as Paladin writes it. You can leave the page; it keeps going.
5. Under **Recruiter assessment**, pick **Strong match**, **Possible match** or **Gaps to discuss**. **AI suggests** marks Paladin’s pick. The report doesn’t show an assessment until you choose one.
6. To change the wording, select **Edit**, click into the report and type, then select **Save**. Or type what you want in the **Revise with AI** box, for example “shorter”, and choose **Keep** or **Discard**.

To report on one call only, select **From latest call** in step 3 instead.

Tip

On the candidate’s page, the **Generate report** button on each opportunity row does the same as steps 2 to 4.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The new report is a **Brief**: about half a page the hiring manager can scan. For a longer one, select **Style: Brief** at the top of the report and choose **Executive** (one page) or **Full**. That makes a new report and keeps the old one.

Every report is listed under **Reports** on the opportunity page, newest first. Each edit is saved as a version; select **History** to see them and **Restore** an older one. To take a copy with you, select **Download DOCX** or **Print / Save PDF**.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **The dialog says “There is nothing on this opportunity yet”.** You can still generate, but the report will be thin. Attach a phone screen transcript or notes on the opportunity page first for a better one.
* **The report says it is a pre-screen assessment.** Nobody has spoken to the candidate through Paladin and no screen transcript is attached. Call the candidate, or attach the transcript, then generate again.
* **You see “Generated while the call was active”.** The call hadn’t ended. Select **Regenerate** once it has.
* **You see “Generation continues in the background”.** The connection dropped but the report is still being written. Check **Reports** on the opportunity page in a minute or two.
* **You see “Only the candidate’s owner or an admin can change this report.”** Ask the candidate’s owner or an admin to make the change.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The steps are the same.

# Send a report to the hiring manager

> Email a candidate report to the job's hiring manager from your own mail app, with the report attached as a Word file.

Paladin starts the email for you. It opens a draft in your own mail app, addressed to the hiring manager, and downloads the report as a Word file for you to attach. You send it yourself, so it comes from your address and lands in your Sent folder.

Before you start

* [Create the report](../create-a-candidate-report/) first.
* The job needs a hiring manager with an email address. See “If something goes wrong” below if it doesn’t have one.

1. Open **Hiring Managers** and select the hiring manager.
2. Select **Send report**. A list of reports on their jobs opens.
3. Select the report you want to send. Your mail app opens a draft, and the report downloads as a `.docx` file.
4. Attach the downloaded file to the draft.
5. Read the draft, change anything you like, and send it.

## What happens next

[Section titled “What happens next”](#what-happens-next)

The hiring manager gets an ordinary email from you. The subject names the candidate, the job and you. The body starts with “Hi” and their first name, then a short summary taken from the report, then “Report attached.” and your name. The report itself is the Word file you attached.

The hiring manager doesn’t need a Paladin account, and there is no link to open. Paladin doesn’t track whether they read it.

## If something goes wrong

[Section titled “If something goes wrong”](#if-something-goes-wrong)

* **Send report is greyed out.** There are two reasons:

  * The hiring manager has no email address. Under **Contact**, select **Add an email**, type the address and press Enter.
  * None of their jobs has a candidate report yet. [Create one](../create-a-candidate-report/) first.

* **The job has no hiring manager.** Open the job. Under **Hiring manager** it says “No hiring manager on this job.” Select **Link / Create**, then pick the person or select **Create new hiring manager**.

* **The job shows a hiring manager with “Convert to record”.** The name was typed on the job before hiring managers were records. Select **Convert to record**, then send from their page.

* **The report you want isn’t in the list.** Open the report itself, select **Download DOCX**, and attach it to an email you write yourself.

* **The report downloads but no email opens.** Your computer may not have a default mail app set. Write the email yourself and attach the downloaded file.

Note

If your team recruits for its own company, Paladin says **Roles** instead of jobs. The steps are the same.
